questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The weather, south Europe, staying in europe.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very helpful to meet with the Coordinators to get my student ID and ask them some questions when i first arrived in Milano. Also because in Italy you dont have to sign up for classes before the semester starts, so i was very stressed about something i didn't have to be stressed about.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I recieved emails about how to sign up for classes and where to go. Also my academic coordinator always answered when i had questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: My friend and I made a post on an apartments in Milano facebook group and found a guy who wanted to rent his apartment to us. That worked well.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Living in milan is a little bit expensive but it was a good experience. Also the public transportation is very good so it was easy to get to school by metro. So if you can, live close to the metro or tram.
But renting from a local gave us an Italian friend from the beginning of the exchange and we were friends and hung out altrough my exchange.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a little confusing at first and most of the courses i thought i would tak where never made. But once i realised that i did not have to register for the courses before they started is was way better. You can try out the courses in the first weeks to find out which courses you want to register for. But be prepared to change your plan for which courses you intend to take when the semester begins.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Everything is very slow and last minute. You have to just decide which classes you want to show up to first week. you dont have to be registered. also class registation didn't open before to days before semester start. So i didnt know what classes would be available until then (because a lot of the classes on the website dont actually get created). So be prepared to adapt and accept that things are a little bit last minute.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: academic coordinator through email mostly

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: The classes i had registered for were not made, so i had to find new classes a week before school started. But everything worked out.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have patience with the italian system. everything will work out so dont stress

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was fine. I think even though i only took masters classes and im on my bachelor it seemed like the level was about the same as the classes my friends where taking at home in Denmark. Also this meant that the classes where mostly easy/fine to follow and a few of them were more difficult but i got some help from the teachers and other students.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A lot more analogue. exams are all closed book, so learning is a lot more about memorizing than about have organized notes. But the teachers were really nice and i definitely recomend showing up to all the classes because it gave me a lot.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Statistics and econometrics, environmental economics, policiy and economics in the agrifood sector, advanced laboratory in financial risk management

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: environmental economics and policiy and economics in the agrifood sector where very interesting courses if you study something with food og agriculture economics. It was very interesting to learn about the agrifood sector in Italy compared to Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were some parties at the univeristy and genereally people all went to the same park after school to drink spritz. But i didn't encounter a lot of clubs or sports.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: i dont know

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: i dont know I didnt experience any that were school related. But i showed up to school every day and became friends with the Italians so we often played Volley after school and played card games and had aperitivo. So i would definetely recommend going to school consistently to get to know the Italians.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I went on a lot of weekend trips to other parts of Italy like como and tuscany on the weekends and it was always amazing experiences.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think it was easy. The Italians i encountered were very proud about their culture so they would always share and make fun of the italian norms and culture.  Italians are always late (even teachers) and apparently it is impolite to wear a hat indoors.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: show up to school and talk to the italians. they were very welcoming at my school. If possible look at the master degrees and see if you can take more classes from the same masters. I had school with the same 30 people for all my classes so it was way easier to get to know the people i went to school with.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Time management. For example my teacher was an hour late for one of my oral exams.
But i dont think overall the cultural differences were very challengning.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their lunch culture. We always had a long lunch and played games. It was definitely also because we had lunch for over an hour every day that i got to become friends with the italians early in my exchange and we started hanging out after school.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. I took all my classes from the same masters degree so i had classes with the same people all week and ended up getting Italians friends.
2. Show up to school every day and get to know the teachers and other students.
3. Dont be shy or reserved

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Even though there are a lot of danish students in Milano try to make local friends as well cause that was the most rewarding part for me.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Definitely getting italian friends and learning so much about their culture and lives. Also because I didnt expect to get them because i had heard that there are so many danish exchange students in Milan so people usually just get danish friends, but i got to have both.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not having enough time. There were more trips i wanted to go on and friends I wanted to hang out with and restaurants i wanted to try...

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
